common.walk_incomplete_desc: These walks did not finish, so finding nothing in them proves nothing: {walks}. Each walk stops after VPSSEC_FS_TIMEOUT seconds (now {timeout}); logs/vpssec.log records why each one stopped.
common.walk_incomplete_fix: Re-run with a longer limit, e.g. VPSSEC_FS_TIMEOUT=300 vpssec audit

cli.cmd_audit: audit    Read-only security scan, generate report
cli.cmd_help: help     Show per-module audit and fix details (use 'help <module>')
cli.opt_strict: --strict         Strict scoring: also count optional hardening checks
cli.opt_fix: --fix=IDS        guide: apply only these fix ids, no menu
cli.ex_fix: Apply one named fix without the menu

preflight.title: Environment Preflight
preflight.os_unsupported_suggestion: Use Debian 12/13, Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04, a RHEL 8/9/10 family distro (Rocky/Alma/CentOS Stream), or Arch
preflight.optional_missing_desc: Working without: {caps}. The audit still runs; these parts fall back or are skipped.

ssh.admin_no_key_desc: No usable key in the authorized_keys files sshd reads: there is none, or the file is refused for its permissions or size
ssh.agent_forwarding_enabled_desc: AllowAgentForwarding={val} (forwarded agent socket can be abused by anyone with root on the remote host)
ssh.allow_tcp_forwarding_enabled_desc: AllowTcpForwarding={val} (recommended: no unless tunneling is intentional)
ssh.gateway_ports_enabled_desc: GatewayPorts={val} (forwarded ports bind to wildcard address, exposing tunneled services)
ssh.ignore_rhosts_disabled_desc: IgnoreRhosts={val} (default is yes; setting no re-enables legacy rhosts-based trust)
ssh.log_level_low_desc: LogLevel={val} (VERBOSE logs fingerprints used at auth time)
ssh.permit_tunnel_enabled_desc: PermitTunnel={val} (allows tun/tap forwarding — network pivot vector)
ssh.permit_user_env_enabled_desc: PermitUserEnvironment={val} (lets authorized_keys inject env vars — privilege escalation primitive)
ssh.strict_modes_disabled_desc: StrictModes={val} (disables permission checks on host keys and ~/.ssh)
ssh.title: SSH Hardening
ssh.not_installed_desc: No sshd on this host, so the SSH checks do not apply; another SSH server (such as dropbear) is not audited
ssh.config_unreadable: sshd could not report its configuration; the SSH checks were skipped
ssh.config_unreadable_desc: sshd -T failed, so no SSH setting could be judged: {error}
ssh.config_unreadable_fix: Run sshd -T as root and fix the error it names (a missing /run/sshd is created when the ssh service starts), then audit again
ssh.desc: Check and harden SSH service configuration
ssh.password_auth_enabled_desc: PasswordAuthentication is yes or not explicitly set
ssh.password_auth_kbdint_desc: Passwords are accepted through keyboard-interactive: KbdInteractiveAuthentication yes with UsePAM yes, and no AuthenticationMethods list needs more than a password
ssh.fix_kbdint_password: Set KbdInteractiveAuthentication no (and PasswordAuthentication no); if keyboard-interactive serves a second factor, require a key first with AuthenticationMethods publickey,keyboard-interactive. vpssec leaves this choice to you
ssh.kbdint_fix_refused: Not changed: passwords would still log in through keyboard-interactive (PAM). Decide on KbdInteractiveAuthentication yourself, then re-run the audit
ssh.root_login_keyonly: Root login allowed (key-only; password auth disabled)
ssh.no_admin_user_desc: No non-root user with sudo privileges found
ssh.rescue_port_notice: Opening rescue port {port} as safety measure
ssh.rescue_port_failed: Cannot open rescue port - aborting SSH changes for safety
ssh.rescue_port_check: Please check if port {port} is available
ssh.rescue_no_free_port: Could not find a free port for the rescue SSH daemon - aborting for safety
ssh.rescue_fw_allowed: Allowed rescue port {port} through the firewall
ssh.rescue_fw_warn: Firewall is active but rescue port {port} was not auto-allowed; make sure it is reachable from your client before confirming
ssh.rescue_fw_unknown: Could not determine the firewall state, so rescue port {port} was not auto-allowed; make sure it is reachable from your client before confirming
ssh.rescue_rule_remove_failed: Could not remove the rescue firewall rule; remove it by hand: {cmd}
ssh.rescue_port_verify: A temporary rescue SSH daemon is now listening on port {port}. Before applying this change, open a SEPARATE terminal and verify you can still log in (e.g. ssh -p {port} your-user@this-host). If you cannot connect, do NOT proceed - this change could otherwise lock you out
ssh.dropin_not_included: {config} has no Include that reads {dir}, so sshd would ignore every SSH fix; add 'Include {dir}/*.conf' near the top of {config}, then run the fix again
ssh.dropin_rolled_back_deleted: Removed the newly written SSH drop-in
ssh.dropin_rolled_back_restored: Restored the previous SSH drop-in from backup
ssh.dropin_rollback_failed: Failed to restore previous SSH drop-in; manual review required
ssh.dropin_rollback_missing: No SSH drop-in backup available for rollback
ssh.effective_mismatch: SSH reloaded but the effective '{key}' is still not '{value}' (sshd -T) - a drop-in or directive read before vpssec's wins; rolled back. Fix the conflicting setting and retry.
ssh.effective_match_override: SSH reloaded and the global '{key}' is now '{value}', but a Match block overrides it for ordinary users (sshd -T -C); rolled back. Change that Match block and retry.
ssh.no_key_user: No admin account could log in by SSH key and then use sudo (that needs a usable password or a NOPASSWD rule). Cannot safely disable password auth.
ssh.only_root_key_warning: Only root has a usable SSH key. Password login will be disabled relying on root's key. Do NOT also disable root login unless a non-root admin has an SSH key, or you will be locked out.
ssh.no_admin_key_pw_off: Password authentication is already disabled and no non-root admin can log in by SSH key and use sudo (a usable password or a NOPASSWD rule). Disabling root login now would remove the last way in. Add an SSH key for a sudo user first.
ssh.add_key_first: Please add an SSH key first: ssh-copy-id user@host
ssh.create_admin_first: Create a sudo user first: adduser newuser && usermod -aG sudo newuser
ssh.gateway_ports_enabled: GatewayPorts enabled (forwarded ports bind to wildcard)
ssh.match_overrides: Match blocks change audited SSH settings for some connections
ssh.match_overrides_desc: The checks above judge what an ordinary user gets; these Match blocks set a different value for the connections they match: {list}
ssh.match_overrides_suggestion: Review each Match block and confirm the override is intended — for example that no Match Address block re-enables root or password login
ssh.no_admin_for_root: No non-root admin could log in and use sudo once root login is off (that needs a login shell, a usable password or SSH key, and a full sudo grant). Cannot safely disable root login.
ssh.reload_after_rollback_failed: Restored the SSH drop-in but could not reload sshd, which keeps the rejected setting until its next reload (systemctl reload ssh)
ssh.rescue_fw_no_source: Could not determine your source IP (console login or stripped environment).
ssh.rescue_fw_ask_cidr: Source IP/CIDR allowed to reach rescue port {port} ('any' = open to the world; empty = add no rule)
ssh.rescue_fw_bad_cidr: Not a valid IP/CIDR: {value} — adding no firewall rule
ssh.admin_no_key_suggestion: Add an SSH public key for {user}
ssh.authkeys_permissions_suggestion: Make each listed path owned by its user (or root) and not group- or world-writable, e.g. chmod go-w <path>
ssh.no_admin_user_suggestion: Create a non-root admin user before disabling root login
ssh.tcp_keepalive_enabled_suggestion: Set TCPKeepAlive to no and rely on ClientAliveInterval instead
ssh.default_port_suggestion: Consider changing to a non-standard port (e.g., 2222, 22222)
ssh.admin_no_key: Admins without a usable SSH key: {user}
ssh.authkeys_permissions: SSH key files have insecure permissions
ssh.authkeys_refused: {path} (mode {mode}, owner {owner}) lets others change {file}; with StrictModes sshd refuses its keys
ssh.verify_main_login: The rescue check tested the temporary daemon, not this change. Keep this session open and, in a NEW terminal, log in as {user} on port {port}. If that fails, run 'vpssec rollback' from this session.
ssh.pubkey_off_no_password_off: Public key authentication is disabled, so turning passwords off would leave sshd no way to log in. Enable public key authentication (ssh.enable_pubkey) first.

ufw.firewall_unknown: Active firewall could not be determined
ufw.firewall_unknown_desc: A firewall status query (ufw status, nft list ruleset or iptables -S INPUT) failed and no active backend was found, so nothing is claimed about whether this host filters traffic; run those commands by hand to see why.
ufw.title: UFW Firewall
ufw.desc: Configure and manage UFW firewall rules
ufw.not_installed_desc: No firewall is filtering inbound traffic, and UFW (the Debian/Ubuntu front-end) is not installed
ufw.disabled_desc: UFW is installed but not enabled
ufw.no_ssh_rule_desc: SSH port {ssh_port} is not explicitly allowed
ufw.rescue_rule_failed: Could not add the rescue rule for {ip}; only the SSH port rules above keep this session open - check them before confirming
ufw.rescue_rule_kept: Kept the rescue rule for {ip}; after confirming a fresh SSH login works, remove it with: ufw delete allow from {ip}
ufw.confirm_ufw_enable: Confirm enable UFW? Ensure SSH rules are correct
ufw.ipv6_bypass: IPv6 bypasses UFW (IPV6=no but host has global IPv6)
ufw.ipv6_bypass_desc: /etc/default/ufw has IPV6=no but the host has a global IPv6 address; v6 packets reach the host without passing UFW filters. Set IPV6=yes and reload UFW.
ufw.fix_enable_ipv6: Set IPV6=yes in /etc/default/ufw, then: ufw disable && ufw enable
ufw.ipv6_no_traffic: IPV6=no in UFW config (host has no global IPv6 address)
ufw.other_firewall_note: Using non-UFW firewall, skipping UFW-specific checks
ufw.no_firewall_desc: System has no active firewall, exposed to network attacks
ufw.default_deny_set: Default incoming policy set to deny
ufw.fix_enable_firewall: Enable a system firewall (firewalld on RHEL, nftables/ufw on Arch)
ufw.operator_ip_unknown: Your SSH source address could not be determined (tmux, screen, mosh or no login record), so no rescue rule is added: only the SSH port rules keep this session open

update.title: System Updates
update.unattended_dryrun_warn: unattended-upgrades dry-run reported an issue; verify the security update origins are matched
update.desc: Check system updates and automatic update configuration
update.apt_locked: Package manager is locked by another process
update.apt_locked_desc: A package operation ({pm}) is already running in another process
update.lock_state_unknown: Could not determine whether the package manager is locked
update.unattended_state_unknown: Could not determine the automatic-update state
update.unattended_state_unknown_desc: unattended-upgrades is installed but its effective state could not be read (apt-config missing or failing, or the config unreadable). This is NOT "disabled" - the question went unanswered.
update.lock_state_unknown_desc: Neither /proc/locks nor lsof could be read, so this host was not checked for an in-flight package operation. This finding is not scored.
update.lock_state_unknown_fix: Install lsof ({cmd}), or make /proc/locks readable, to have this checked
update.lock_state_unknown_desc_dnf: pgrep is not installed, so this host was not checked for a running dnf, yum or PackageKit. This finding is not scored.
update.lock_state_unknown_fix_dnf: Install pgrep ({cmd}) to have this checked
update.lock_state_unknown_desc_other: vpssec has no lock check for this host's package manager, so it was not checked for an in-flight package operation. This finding is not scored.
update.lock_state_unknown_fix_other: Before installing or upgrading packages, make sure no other package operation is running
update.installing_unattended_for_security: Installing unattended-upgrades to apply the security updates (daily automatic updates stay off)...
update.security_aborted_install_uu_first: Security update aborted. Install manually: apt install unattended-upgrades, then re-run.
update.auto_upgrades_write_failed: Could not write {file}; automatic updates were not enabled
update.uu_dropin_write_failed: Could not write {file}; the security-only origins were not applied
update.security_applied_revert_hint: Rollback restores config files, not installed packages. What was upgraded is listed in /var/log/apt/history.log
update.reboot_state_unknown: Could not determine whether a reboot is required
update.reboot_state_unknown_desc: None of the distribution's reboot signals answered, and there is no installed kernel package to compare the running kernel with (usual in a container, whose kernel belongs to the host). This finding is not scored.
update.check_failed_desc: The package manager's update query failed (broken sources, cold metadata cache, or missing tool). This is NOT "no updates" — the question went unanswered.
update.check_failed_fix: Refresh the package index ({cmd}) and re-run the audit
update.check_failed_fix_generic: Refresh the package index with the system package manager and re-run the audit
update.index_stale: Pending updates unknown: the package index is not current
update.index_never_refreshed_desc: No refresh of the package index was found (fresh images often ship none), so the update query had nothing to compare against. vpssec does not refresh it during an audit.
update.index_stale_desc: The package index was last refreshed {days} days ago, so "no pending updates" would describe that day, not today. vpssec does not refresh it during an audit.
update.apt_locked_suggestion: Wait for the other package operation to finish, then re-run the audit; do not delete the lock files
update.updates_available_suggestion: Apply pending updates with the system package manager
update.reboot_required_suggestion: Schedule a system reboot to apply kernel/security updates
update.unattended_refresh_disabled: the package index is not refreshed on a schedule (apt-daily.timer or APT::Periodic::Update-Package-Lists is off), so automatic upgrades keep reading the index of the last manual refresh
update.unattended_periodic_off: auto-update is installed but not set to apply updates
update.unattended_not_effective: auto-update mechanism installed but not effective

docker.all_root_containers_desc: All containers are running as root user
docker.default_bridge_icc_enabled_desc: Inter-container communication on the docker0 bridge is enabled. If any container is compromised it can reach every other container on the default bridge.
docker.host_network_used_desc: Containers: {list}. These share the host network namespace (bind any port, see all host traffic). Review whether each container actually needs host network.
docker.no_live_restore_desc: Containers will stop during Docker daemon restart
docker.no_new_privileges_disabled_desc: Containers can gain new privileges by default
docker.secrets_in_env_desc: Containers (kinds + counts only; raw values withheld): {sample}. Any process with docker socket access reads these via 'docker inspect'.
docker.some_root_containers_desc: Some containers are running as root user
docker.unlimited_memory_desc: Containers: {list}. Without --memory a runaway / leaking container can OOM the host. Acceptable on single-app servers; address on multi-tenant hosts.
docker.title: Docker Security
docker.desc: Check Docker container and network security configuration
docker.added_capabilities_suggestion: Remove each --cap-add (compose: cap_add) the service does not need and recreate the container; SYS_ADMIN and ALL are close to --privileged
docker.review_template: Review and adapt the template for your services
docker.daemon_invalid_json: Refusing to edit {path}: existing file is not valid JSON. Fix it manually first.
docker.daemon_update_failed: Failed to update Docker daemon configuration; original file left unchanged
docker.confirm_restart: Restart the Docker daemon now so the change takes effect? live-restore is off, so every running container is stopped, and containers without a restart policy stay stopped. no-new-privileges applies only to containers created afterwards.
docker.restart_failed: Failed to restart Docker; check 'systemctl status docker' and 'journalctl -u docker'
docker.restart_skipped: Docker NOT restarted; new setting takes effect on next restart
docker.sock_perms_loose_desc: Mode {mode} lets non-root/non-docker-group users talk to the Docker API, which is equivalent to root on the host. Typical cause: a tutorial told the user to `chmod a+rw /var/run/docker.sock` to bypass a permission error.
docker.sock_perms_fix: Restore to 0660 root:docker (chown root:docker /var/run/docker.sock; chmod 660 /var/run/docker.sock) and add intended users to the docker group instead.
docker.seccomp_unconfined_desc: Containers bypassing the default seccomp profile: {containers}. Full syscall surface is exposed, undoing Docker's default syscall filter.
docker.seccomp_fix: Remove --security-opt seccomp=unconfined from the run/compose config, or supply a scoped profile with --security-opt seccomp=/path/to/profile.json.
docker.no_seccomp_unconfined: No containers running with seccomp disabled
docker.userns_not_enabled_desc: Containers run with container-root mapped to host-root. userns-remap is available in every modern Docker build but must be enabled daemon-wide to take effect.
docker.userns_fix: Set `"userns-remap": "default"` in /etc/docker/daemon.json and restart the daemon. Note: changes container image storage paths; review before enabling on a production host.
docker.check_host_network: Checking containers with host network namespace
docker.no_host_network: No containers using host network namespace
docker.fix_host_network: Recreate the container without --network=host; use a user-defined bridge or default bridge unless host networking is genuinely required (VPN, monitoring agents)
docker.default_bridge_icc_enabled: Default-bridge ICC enabled (Docker default; allows lateral movement)
docker.fix_default_bridge_icc: Add "icc": false to /etc/docker/daemon.json and restart docker; use user-defined networks for containers that need to communicate
docker.check_secrets_in_env: Scanning container env vars for embedded credentials
docker.secrets_in_env: {count} container(s) with embedded credentials in env vars
docker.no_env_secrets: No embedded credential patterns in container env vars
docker.fix_secrets_in_env: Rotate the exposed credentials; use docker secrets, mounted secret files, or cloud-provider secret stores instead of -e/--env
docker.memory_limits_set: All running containers have memory limits configured
docker.fix_unlimited_memory: Re-run each container with --memory=<size> (e.g. --memory=512m) or set mem_limit in docker-compose
docker.daemon_unreachable_desc: Found {found}, but no daemon answered docker info, so no container check ran: vpssec inspects only what root's docker command reaches.
docker.daemon_unreachable_fix: Start the Docker daemon if it should be running. Rootless Docker can be reviewed as root by pointing the docker CLI at the user's socket, e.g. DOCKER_HOST=unix:///run/user/<uid>/docker.sock docker ps; Podman with podman ps
docker.exposed_ports_suggestion: Use reverse proxy or bind to 127.0.0.1
docker.privileged_containers_suggestion: Remove --privileged flag, use specific capabilities instead
docker.root_containers_suggestion: Use USER directive in Dockerfile or --user flag
docker.no_new_privileges_disabled: Docker no-new-privileges not set as default
docker.confirm_restart_live: Restart the Docker daemon now so the change takes effect? live-restore is on, so running containers keep running. no-new-privileges applies only to containers created afterwards.
docker.reloaded: Docker daemon reloaded; running containers were not touched
docker.reload_failed: Failed to reload Docker; check 'systemctl status docker' and 'journalctl -u docker'
docker.daemon_flag_set: {flag} is already on dockerd's command line (its systemd unit or DOCKER_OPTS); change it there. Setting it in daemon.json as well would stop dockerd from starting.
docker.podman_daemon_not_checked: Docker daemon settings not checked: docker is Podman
docker.podman_daemon_not_checked_desc: The docker command is Podman (podman-docker), which has no Docker daemon: live-restore, no-new-privileges, userns-remap and default-bridge ICC are dockerd settings, so they were not checked. Container checks still ran.

nginx.client_header_timeout_high_desc: client_header_timeout={cht_raw} (CIS 5.2.1: ≤10s; nginx default 60s leaves Slowloris vulnerable)
nginx.dos_hardening_ok_desc: client_header/body/send_timeout, keepalive_timeout, rate limiting, and reset_timedout_connection all match CIS / nginx-mitigation recommendations
nginx.no_rate_limiting_desc: No limit_req_zone directive in effective config — public-facing nginx benefits from per-IP request rate caps to throttle brute-force and scraping attacks
nginx.reset_timedout_connection_off_desc: reset_timedout_connection is off (nginx default). Enabling forcibly closes connections with misbehaving / slow clients, accelerating slowloris recovery
nginx.title: Nginx Catchall
nginx.desc: Configure Nginx default deny rules to prevent information leakage
nginx.no_catchall_desc: Neither port 80 nor port 443 has a default_server block returning 444. Connections for hostnames this server does not host fall through to whichever server block nginx selects, exposing real certificates and hostnames. A default_server may well exist — what is missing is one that rejects unknown names.
nginx.catchall_both_desc: Default-server return-444 catchall present on both port 80 and port 443
nginx.catchall_partial_80_desc: Port 80 has a default_server returning 444, but port 443 does not. HTTPS connections to unknown hostnames will fall through to whichever 443 server block nginx selects, exposing real certificates and hostnames.
nginx.catchall_partial_443_desc: Port 443 has a default_server returning 444, but port 80 does not. HTTP connections to unknown hostnames will fall through to whichever 80 server block nginx selects.
nginx.reload_failed_staged: Config is valid but 'systemctl reload nginx' failed: the catch-all is staged on disk but NOT live. Fix nginx and reload manually — the host is still exposed until you do.
nginx.sites_enabled_missing: {dir} does not exist, so nothing would read a catchall placed there. Not applying the fix.
nginx.sites_enabled_hint: This host does not use the sites-enabled layout. To use it, add 'include {dir}/*.conf;' to the http block of nginx.conf and re-run; otherwise add the catchall to whichever directory your nginx.conf includes.
nginx.catchall_write_failed: Could not write the catchall configuration to {file}
nginx.ssl_dir_failed: Could not create the certificate directory {dir}
nginx.cert_generate_failed: Could not generate the self-signed certificate {file}. The 443 catchall references it, so nginx would refuse to load.
nginx.cert_chmod_failed: Could not restrict permissions on the private key {file}; refusing to leave it world-readable
nginx.catchall_conf_kept: Left {file} in place — it existed before this run, so removing it is not this fix's call. Use 'vpssec rollback' to restore the original.
nginx.catchall_postcondition_failed: Nginx reloaded but the catchall is still not in force (state: {state}). Another default_server may be winning, or nginx.conf may not include sites-enabled.
nginx.config_unreadable: Nginx configuration fails its own test
nginx.config_unreadable_desc: nginx -t rejects the configuration, so the checks that read it were skipped: {error}
nginx.config_unreadable_fix: Run nginx -t, fix the error it names, then audit again
nginx.catchall_80_desc: Port 80 has a default_server returning 444. Nginx serves nothing on port 443, so nothing there needs one.
nginx.catchall_80_only: Nginx serves nothing on port 443, so only the port-80 catchall is written
nginx.catchall_not_live: The catchall is on disk and nginx reloaded, yet an unknown hostname on port 80 still gets an answer: the running nginx did not take the new configuration. Check nginx's error log; a port it could not bind is the usual cause.
nginx.catchall_unverified: An unknown hostname on port 80 got neither an answer nor a closed connection within 3 seconds, so whether the catchall is live cannot be confirmed.
nginx.fix_dos_timeouts: Set timeout to ≤10s in /etc/nginx/nginx.conf http block
nginx.fix_dos_rate_limit: Add: limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=perip:10m rate=10r/s; then apply with limit_req zone=perip burst=20 nodelay; in location blocks
nginx.fix_dos_reset_timedout: Add: reset_timedout_connection on; to /etc/nginx/nginx.conf http block

baseline.apparmor_enabled_desc: AppArmor enabled: {enforced} profiles enforcing, {complain} in complain mode
baseline.apparmor_many_complain_desc: Many AppArmor profiles in complain mode (not enforcing)
baseline.no_mac_system_desc: No Mandatory Access Control system (SELinux/AppArmor) detected
baseline.mac_host_managed_desc: In a container, AppArmor or SELinux confinement is set up by the host kernel and the container manager. Nothing inside the container can enable it, so this is listed, not scored.
baseline.mac_host_managed_ok_desc: {state}. In a container the host kernel and the container manager set this policy, so it is listed, not scored.
baseline.selinux_many_denials_desc: High number of SELinux denials may indicate misconfiguration
baseline.selinux_permissive_desc: SELinux is in permissive mode - violations are logged but not enforced
baseline.title: Baseline Hardening
baseline.desc: Check and configure system security baseline
baseline.apparmor_disabled_desc: AppArmor is installed but has no profile loaded: it is not enabled, or its profiles were never loaded
baseline.mac_host_managed: No MAC policy is enforced inside this container; the host kernel sets it
baseline.mac_host_managed_ok: A MAC policy is enforced in this container; the host kernel sets it
baseline.selinux_config_restore: Unexpected {file} layout (no SELINUX= line); left unchanged - set SELINUX=enforcing manually
baseline.selinux_config_write_failed: Could not write {file}; SELinux is enforcing now but will not be after a reboot
baseline.selinux_runtime_only: SELinux is enforcing now, but {file} does not exist so the setting will not survive a reboot - configure SELinux persistently by hand
baseline.selinux_enforcing_failed: Failed to set SELinux enforcing mode
baseline.unused_services_desc: Enabled services: {services}. These (cups, avahi-daemon, bluetooth, etc.) are commonly unneeded on a headless server but may be legitimate on print/media/desktop hosts.
baseline.review_unused_services: Review whether you rely on any of these services before disabling them
baseline.apparmor_install_failed: Failed to install the AppArmor packages (apparmor, apparmor-utils)
baseline.apparmor_profiles_disabled_desc: These profiles are symlinked into the disable directory, so they appear in neither the enforcing nor the complain count: {list}
baseline.apparmor_profiles_disabled_fix: Review {dir}; remove the symlink and reload the profile to re-enable it
baseline.insecure_services_active_suggestion: Disable the service (systemctl disable --now <name>) and remove the package ({remove_hint})
baseline.integrity_missing_suggestion_generic: Install a file integrity tool (AIDE, Tripwire or Samhain)
baseline.apparmor_many_complain_suggestion: Review and set profiles to enforce mode
baseline.no_mac_system_suggestion: Install and enable AppArmor or SELinux
baseline.mac_host_managed_suggestion: Ask the host operator or provider whether this container runs under an AppArmor or SELinux profile
baseline.selinux_config_disabled: SELinux is configured as disabled in {file}

logging.title: Logging & Audit
logging.audit_rules_pending: Audit rules written but not loaded yet (auditd inactive); they apply at next auditd start or reboot
logging.desc: Check system logging and audit configuration
logging.journald_volatile_desc: Logs lost on reboot, recommend enabling persistent storage
logging.journald_volatile_syslog_desc: The journal itself is not kept across reboots; {daemon} still writes the system logs to files under /var/log, and those are. Persistent storage keeps the journal as well.
logging.logrotate_missing_desc: Recommend configuring log rotation to prevent disk space exhaustion
logging.auditd_running: Audit daemon running with rules configured
logging.auditd_no_rules: Audit daemon running but no rules configured
logging.auditd_no_rules_desc: No audit rules configured, recommend adding rules
logging.auditd_not_running_desc: auditd can record system security events, recommend enabling
logging.auditd_not_installed: Audit daemon not installed (optional but recommended)
logging.ssh_logs_high: {count} SSH login failures in last 24h (possible brute force)
logging.ssh_logs_warning_desc: {count} failed attempts in 24h, possible attack in progress
logging.journald_flush_failed: journald did not answer the flush; the journal moves to disk when journald next starts
logging.journald_limits_next_start: The size and retention limits in {file} take effect when journald next starts (at the latest, the next boot)
logging.audit_immutable_hint: For compliance / forensic integrity, consider uncommenting '-e 2' in /etc/audit/rules.d/99-vpssec.rules and rebooting; once applied, audit rules cannot be modified without another reboot.
logging.journal_unreadable: Could not read the systemd journal
logging.journal_unreadable_desc: journalctl failed, so failed SSH logins and sudo activity could not be counted. This is not evidence of quiet — the journal went unread.
logging.journal_unreadable_fix: Check that systemd-journald is running and journal files exist under /var/log/journal or /run/log/journal

webapp.desc: Check web server and application security configuration
webapp.add_security_headers: Add security headers to Nginx configuration
webapp.add_hsts: Add HSTS header for HTTPS enforcement
webapp.disable_autoindex: Set autoindex off; in Nginx configuration
webapp.disable_weak_ssl: Allow only TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3: set ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3; in each server listed, or, for a value set in the http block, in the http block of nginx.conf
webapp.update_ciphers: Remove the weak ciphers from ssl_ciphers where the finding says it is set: the server, or the http block of nginx.conf
webapp.disable_functions: Add dangerous functions to disable_functions in php.ini
webapp.set_open_basedir: Set open_basedir to restrict PHP file access
webapp.remove_sensitive: Remove or restrict access to sensitive files
webapp.remove_backups: Remove backup files from web-accessible directories
webapp.server_tokens_fixed: server_tokens off added and Nginx reloaded
webapp.reload_failed: Config is valid but 'systemctl reload nginx' failed: the change is written to disk but NOT live. Reload nginx manually.
webapp.nginx_restored: Restored Nginx configuration from backup after the change failed validation
webapp.include_headers: Include in server blocks if not automatic
webapp.hsts_warning: Uncomment and add to HTTPS server blocks manually
webapp.other_webserver: Web server present but not audited: {server}
webapp.other_webserver_desc: vpssec audits Nginx and Apache only. {server} is running on this host and none of the web-server checks were applied to it.
webapp.other_webserver_fix: Audit this web server's configuration by hand, or check whether the host still needs it
webapp.fix_hsts_always: Add the 'always' parameter to the Strict-Transport-Security add_header so error responses carry it too
webapp.template_replaced: Replaced the existing {file}; the previous file is backed up at {backup}
webapp.nginx_not_on_path: nginx is running, but its binary is not on PATH: not audited
webapp.nginx_not_on_path_desc: An nginx process is running, but no nginx binary is on PATH (a source build installs to /usr/local/nginx/sbin), so none of the nginx checks ran here or in the nginx module, whose "not installed" line does not hold for this host.
webapp.nginx_not_on_path_fix: Re-run with its directory on PATH, e.g. sudo env PATH="$PATH:/usr/local/nginx/sbin" ./vpssec audit

error.root_required: Root privileges required to run this command
error.cannot_read_critical: Cannot read user input for critical confirmation - aborting
error.module_failed_desc: The {module} audit stopped partway (exit {rc}); its remaining checks were never evaluated. This report is incomplete for that module.
error.module_failed_load_desc: The {module} module failed to load; none of its checks ran. This report is incomplete for that module.
error.module_failed_fix: Re-run with --debug and check logs/vpssec.log; report the failure if it persists.
error.malformed_check_fix: Please report to vpssec maintainers with the relevant logs/vpssec.log entry
error.malformed_check_desc: A module emitted invalid JSON for a check. Raw payload (first 500 bytes): {raw}
error.already_running_pid: Another vpssec instance is already running (PID {pid}).
error.already_running: Another vpssec instance is already running.
error.already_running_hint: Wait for it to finish, or stop it: kill {pid}
error.oneshot_stateful: '{cmd}' is not available through the one-line runner: it deletes its temporary directory on exit, and a fix's backups with it. Install vpssec with install.sh, then run: sudo vpssec {cmd}
error.supported_platforms: Supported (audit): Debian 12/13, Ubuntu 22.04/24.04/26.04, RHEL 8/9/10 family (Rocky/Alma/CentOS Stream), Arch. Automated fixes (guide): Debian/Ubuntu only.
error.confirm_timeout: No answer within {seconds}s - treated as NO
error.module_failed_emit_desc: At least one {module} check could not be recorded (see logs/vpssec.log), so its result is missing. This report is incomplete for that module.
error.bad_fs_timeout: VPSSEC_FS_TIMEOUT must be a whole number of seconds greater than 0 (got "{value}")

fixwarn.baseline.selinux_disabled: Enabling SELinux requires system reboot and may cause service issues
fixwarn.cloud.agents_found: Review if monitoring agents are needed
fixwarn.docker.default_bridge_icc_enabled: Changing daemon ICC setting restarts dockerd and disconnects containers
fixwarn.docker.exposed_ports: Port exposure is an architecture decision
fixwarn.docker.host_network_used: Each container with --network=host needs case-by-case review; removing it may break the container's intended function
fixwarn.docker.seccomp_unconfined: Reverting seccomp=unconfined requires understanding why it was set
fixwarn.docker.secrets_in_env: Credentials must be rotated externally; vpssec cannot mutate running container environments safely
fixwarn.docker.sock_perms_loose: Changing socket perms can break running tooling; review users in the docker group first
fixwarn.docker.unlimited_memory: Memory limits must be set at container start time; vpssec will not restart running containers
fixwarn.docker.userns_not_enabled: Enabling userns-remap changes storage paths and breaks some tooling
fixwarn.filesystem.dangerous_caps: Review file capabilities; remove if not needed
fixwarn.filesystem.suspicious_sgid: Review and remove SGID bit if not needed
fixwarn.filesystem.suspicious_suid: Review and remove SUID bit if not needed
fixwarn.malware.hidden_processes: CRITICAL: System may be compromised by rootkit
fixwarn.malware.mining_pool_connection: Block mining pool and remove malware
fixwarn.malware.webshell: Remove webshell and investigate access logs
fixwarn.ssh.no_access_control: Restrict access with AllowUsers/AllowGroups manually (wrong values can lock you out)
fixwarn.ssh.no_admin_user: Create admin user manually before disabling root
fixwarn.ufw.permissive_rules: Review and tighten overly-permissive firewall rules manually
fixwarn.update.apt_locked: Wait for the other package operation to finish; never delete the lock files
fixwarn.users.empty_password: CRITICAL: Set passwords or lock accounts
fixwarn.users.history_insecure: Shell history hardening is an operator preference
fixwarn.users.nopasswd_sudo: Review NOPASSWD sudoers entries manually (do not auto-modify sudoers)
fixwarn.users.system_with_shell: Review if shell access is needed
fixwarn.users.uid0_found: CRITICAL: Review UID 0 accounts - may be backdoors
fixwarn.webapp.backup_files: Remove backup files from web root
fixwarn.baseline.disable_unused: Stops/disables services flagged as unused (e.g. avahi/cups); review before applying
fixwarn.baseline.enable_apparmor: Enforces all installed AppArmor profiles immediately; may cause denials against a running service
fixwarn.baseline.selinux_set_enforcing: May cause service denials if SELinux policies not configured properly
fixwarn.docker.enable_live_restore: Reloads the Docker daemon (no restart); any other pending reloadable daemon.json change takes effect too
fixwarn.docker.enable_no_new_privileges: Restarts the Docker daemon, which stops every running container unless live-restore is on; applies only to containers created afterwards
fixwarn.fail2ban.configure_ssh_jail: Writes /etc/fail2ban/jail.d/99-vpssec-sshd.local; existing files are kept, but it overrides the bantime/findtime/maxretry and log backend you set for the sshd jail in jail.local or jail.d/*.conf (its ignoreip is kept, with loopback and your SSH address added), and sets banaction for every jail to the firewall tool this host has
fixwarn.fail2ban.enable_ssh_jail: Writes /etc/fail2ban/jail.d/99-vpssec-sshd.local; existing files are kept, but it overrides the bantime/findtime/maxretry and log backend you set for the sshd jail in jail.local or jail.d/*.conf (its ignoreip is kept, with loopback and your SSH address added), and sets banaction for every jail to the firewall tool this host has
fixwarn.kernel.harden_ipv6: May drop IPv6 connectivity on hosts that obtain their address/route via Router Advertisements (SLAAC)
fixwarn.kernel.harden_kernel: Disables unprivileged user namespaces (breaks Docker rootless / podman / Chrome sandbox) and restricts SysRq
fixwarn.kernel.harden_network: May affect container networking (Docker/LXC); IPv6 RA settings are skipped on SLAAC hosts to preserve connectivity; a weaker value in ufw's sysctl file, which every ufw reload re-applies, is overridden there too
fixwarn.nginx.add_catchall: Adds a default server that closes requests for unknown hostnames and bare-IP requests on port 80, and on 443 when nginx already serves 443
fixwarn.ssh.harden_algorithms: Removes SHA-1/MD5 MACs and SHA-1 key exchange from the defaults: clients offering nothing newer can no longer connect
fixwarn.timezone.set_timezone: Prompts for a new system timezone; log timestamps and cron schedules shift with it
fixwarn.alerts.setup_config: Asks for a webhook URL and an email address, then writes the alert config and monitor scripts
fixwarn.update.enable_unattended: Enables automatic unattended installation of security updates
fixwarn.update.install_unattended: Installs and enables automatic unattended security updates
fixwarn.webapp.nginx_hsts: Once enabled, browsers will refuse HTTP
fixwarn.ssh.disable_password_auth: Can lock you out if SSH key not configured properly
fixwarn.ssh.disable_root_login: Can lock you out if no admin user exists
fixwarn.ufw.enable: Can lock you out if SSH not allowed
fixwarn.ufw.set_default_deny: Flips the firewall to deny-all inbound; can drop running services not explicitly allowed, and can lock you out if the SSH rule is wrong
fixwarn.update.apply_security: May break system packages or services
fixwarn.ssh.set_max_auth_tries: Lowers MaxAuthTries to 4: every key a client offers counts as an attempt, so one whose agent offers four or more other keys first is disconnected; set IdentitiesOnly yes with the right IdentityFile on such clients

fixtmpl.docker.generate_proxy_template: A reverse-proxy template was written for you to review and deploy; the ports stay exposed until you do
fixtmpl.cloudflared.generate_config: A tunnel config template was written; copy it to /etc/cloudflared and create the tunnel to finish
fixtmpl.backup.generate_templates: Backup script templates were written; no backup tool is installed and nothing is scheduled yet
fixtmpl.alerts.setup_config: The alert config and monitor scripts were written; install the monitors as their README shows (PAM hook, cron) to start receiving alerts, and add a webhook or email to the config if you skipped it
fixtmpl.webapp.nginx_ssl_protocols: A hardened SSL snippet was written to nginx snippets/; it does nothing until you include it in your server block
fixtmpl.webapp.nginx_ssl_ciphers: A hardened SSL snippet was written to nginx snippets/; it does nothing until you include it in your server block
fixtmpl.webapp.nginx_hsts: An HSTS template was written with the header commented out; uncomment it in your HTTPS server blocks once you are sure every site is HTTPS-only
